messages:
ryan (support): Hey team — Sandpine reported a sudden p99 tail on text-generation-endpoint starting ~2026-03-14 21:00 UTC. They see lots of 5-12s calls on /v1/generate for model=gptx-small. Customer says traffic pattern didn't change. attaching their sample request below.

maya (customer-success): cc @ana @jun — Sandpine is on a large PLG plan, business-critical flows hitting p99. They asked for immediate mitigation and an ETA.

ryan (support): Repro steps from customer (they ran this from their integration):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REW_TOKEN"
  -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: sandpine-tn-44"
  -d '{"model":"gptx-small","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":512}'
```
Responses: most are 180-400ms but a subset spike to >5s. They included a small sample of slow traces with request IDs.

ana (typo) -> ana (eng-sre): I pulled the request-ids they gave and checked traces in tracing-prod. The slow requests line up with these patterns: (a) long wait queue on router (~3-4s), (b) worker exec ~1s, (c) occasional KV-cache miss adds ~1s. Looks like queuing/backpressure on the edge for tenant sandpine-tn-44.

ana: Linking grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving/p99-latency?orgId=1&var-tenant=sandpine-tn-44 :eyes:

ana (eng-sre): Quick checks I ran:
- Checked reservation/quotas: sandpine has no reserved capacity.
- Token rate to /generate peaked at ~220 rps at 21:05 UTC, sustained ~60rps baseline.
- Router queue depth showed occasional spikes to 120 concurrent queued at the router pod (our SLO is 50 for that class).
- No errors in worker pods, CPU/GPU utilization normal, but router CPU at 95% on one AZ.

jun (eng-platform): Do we have noisy neighbour evidence? Could be another tenant bursting on same router shard. I can query routing logs for tenant distribution.

ana (eng-sre): I searched router logs for that timeframe: there was a tenant "clamor-ops" with a short burst of many small requests (embeddings + short-chat) around 21:03 which correlated with router queue growth. The router shards are per-AZ and per-flavor, so sandpine and clamor-ops share the same shard right now.

maya (customer-success): Sandpine is asking for a short-term fix (they're ok with a safety-net allowlist or temporary reserved slot while we investigate). They also asked if we can throttle the noisy tenant if needed.

ana (eng-sre): Proposed mitigations (short term):
1) Add sandpine to per-tenant high-priority allowlist on the router for 24h (gives them priority in queueing).
2) Apply a soft per-tenant ingress cap to clamor-ops to reduce head-of-line blocking (rate limit to 120 rps for 30m).
3) Create a small reservation (1x compute slot) for sandpine for 24-72h if they approve.

jun (eng-platform): I can push the allowlist rule and the per-tenant throttle. Need tenant IDs and a quick change window. Will run infra change via deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: /infra-change apply --target=router-shard-12 --change="allowlist:add sandpine-tn-44 priority=high ttl=24h" --requester=jun

deploy-bot: change queued, running preflight checks...

deploy-bot: rollout started (change-id: d7f3c2).

ryan (support): Notifying Sandpine: "We're applying a temporary priority allowlist for your tenant and throttling a noisy neighbor. We'll monitor and follow up in 1 hour with metrics."

maya (customer-success): Sandpine confirmed they saw immediate improvement for some calls but still occasional >1s tails. They asked what exactly the allowlist does. I explained it's queue-priority, not compute reservation.

ana (eng-sre): After allowlist and throttle deployed: observation at 21:18 UTC -> router queue depth fell from ~120 -> ~15 for sandpine, p99 for sandpine dropped from ~6.2s -> ~480ms in the first 10m. KV-cache miss rate still accounts for ~80-120ms when it occurs.

ana (eng-sre): Key snippet from tracing showing before/after (timeouts truncated):
```
BEFORE: router.wait 3.8s -> worker.exec 1.2s -> model.kv_miss 1.1s -> total ~6.1s
AFTER: router.wait 0.25s -> worker.exec 0.9s -> model.kv_miss 0.12s -> total ~1.27s
```

jun (eng-platform): Follow-ups:
- I'll keep the allowlist for 24h and monitor.
- If noise recurs, we should move sandpine to a small reservation (1 slot) for predictability.
- We also need to rebalance router shards so high-volume tenants aren't co-located with unpredictable burst tenants. Filed infra ticket INF-2026 to track shard rebalance.

maya (customer-success): Sandpine asked for a written RCA and whether we can guarantee no regressions. They also inquired about a permanent option (reservation). I told them we'll propose a short-term reservation plus next-week follow-up.

ana (eng-sre): Action items:
- [ana] Monitor p99/p95 dashboards for sandpine for next 24h and report hourly for first 4h.
- [jun] Keep allowlist + throttle in place for 24h, prepare reservation quote.
- [maya] Send customer summary, include tracing snippets and ETA for reservation pricing.

ryan (support): Customer update sent at 21:27 UTC. They replied :thumbsup: and asked if we can also provide a list of their slow request-ids for auditing. I forwarded the traces.

deploy-bot: infra-change d7f3c2 succeeded on router-shard-12 (ap-south-1).

ana (eng-sre): 22:05 UTC checkpoint: p99 stabilized at ~260-320ms, occasional blips to ~700ms during a separate cache eviction event. Not ideal but within SLO impact tolerance.

maya (customer-success): Customer extremely relieved. They accepted a 72h temporary reservation offer while we evaluate longer-term options.

jun (eng-platform): Reservation created (res-req-558) pending billing approval. I flagged finance for expedited short-term billing so the reservation can spin up quickly.

ryan (support): Closing note: This was caused by co-located bursty tenant + router shard queue limits. Short-term mitigations (allowlist + throttle + small reservation) worked. Long-term: shard rebalancing and tenant-aware placement + clearer reservation UI to avoid surprise noisy neighbors.

ana (eng-sre): Will collect final 24h metrics and post an RCA in #postmortems once the reservation runs and we confirm stable p99.

maya (customer-success): Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the customer tomorrow with the one-pager and the reservation quote.

ryan (support): marking thread resolved for now. If p99 creeps back up I'll reopen and tag eng-sre. :white_check_mark:
